items.headline: Stocks bounce back Monday: Dow up about 1.1%, S&P 500 0.6%, Nasdaq 0.7%
items.note: One report (the only one I found with Monday's closes, so treat the figures as approximate) says a sharp drop in oil prices and a tech rebound after Friday's sell-off drove the gains. Investors were also positioning ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections.

items.headline: Oil falls more than 7% as Middle East tensions ease
items.note: The same report says crude dropped after Secretary of State Rubio said no decision had been made to attack Iran. Cheaper oil eases inflation worries, which matters for where interest rates go.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO: public filing is in, but no date or price range yet
items.note: The public S-1 was filed Oct 26 for a Nasdaq listing under 'ANT'. The earliest the roadshow can start is Nov 10, and reports differ on whether trading comes the week of Nov 16 or before Thanksgiving. None of these dates is confirmed.

items.headline: Leaks hint at Anthropic 'Fable 5.5' and OpenAI 'GPT-6.2 Astra'
items.note: Both come from unnamed usage data and a catalog entry that was quickly removed. Neither company has confirmed anything, so treat it as rumor.

items.headline: Oracle falls more than 5% after plans to sell $10B in stock and $10B in bonds for AI
items.note: Funding AI data centers by issuing new shares and debt is a theme to watch: investors worry about who pays for the spending. This comes from a single report.

items.headline: Amazon gains more than 4% Monday after a rough post-earnings Friday
items.note: The stock had slipped 1.4% on Friday after Q3 earnings and revenue missed estimates. The bounce helped lift the Dow and Nasdaq.

items.headline: Fed's Collins says another rate hike is possible before the end of 2026; jobs report due Friday
items.note: Boston Fed President Collins pointed to a solid economy and the goal of getting inflation back to target. The October jobs report comes out Friday, Nov 6 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

items.headline: AI/ML job postings up 88% year over year in Dice's September data
items.note: Overall tech postings grew just 17%, so the demand is concentrated in AI and machine learning, which is where you're aiming. Figure from a Dice summary page I only saw in search results.

learn.explain: Oil is a commodity, a raw material traded on global markets, and it feeds into the cost of gasoline, shipping and plastics. When oil jumps, prices across the economy tend to rise, which pushes inflation up. When oil falls, as it did on Monday after Middle East tensions eased, inflation worries fade. The Fed watches inflation when deciding interest rates, so a big oil move can shift stocks. Cheaper oil helps most companies, but it hurts oil producers.
learn.try: Look up the price of Brent crude and WTI (the two main oil benchmarks) and see how they differ.
